# Connect GitHub Clone UI to Local Filesystem

This plan outlines how to link the **GitHub Clone UI** to actual physical files on your hard drive. 

Currently, the files displayed in the web application (like `README.md`, `src/physics.py`, etc.) are hardcoded string arrays inside [mockData.js](file:///c:/Users/ravil/.gemini/antigravity-ide/scratch/github-clone/data/mockData.js). This means editing files in your IDE does not change what displays in the web application.

We will create a physical `repos/` directory on your disk, move the files there, and update the build system so it dynamically crawls your disk directories to build the application database.

---

## Proposed Changes

We will restructure the project to look like this:
```
github-clone/
  ├── dist/               # Compiled bundle
  ├── components/         # UI Components
  ├── data/
  │    └── mockData.js    # User profile data (repos list generated dynamically)
  ├── repos/              # Physical Git Repositories
  │    ├── antigravity-core/
  │    │    ├── repo.json # Metadata (Stars, description, issues, PRs)
  │    │    ├── README.md
  │    │    ├── src/
  │    │    └── tests/
  │    ├── glassmorphic-ui/
  │    └── portfolio-website/
  ├── build.ps1           # Updated to compile disk files into dist/index.html
  └── index.html
```

### 1. Create Repository Directories and Files

We will create a `repos/` folder and populate it with the three existing repositories:
*   **antigravity-core**: Includes Python simulation files.
*   **glassmorphic-ui**: Includes CSS and demo JS.
*   **portfolio-website**: Includes the HTML homepage.

We will also add a `repo.json` to each repository folder to store GitHub-specific metadata that is not part of a standard filesystem (e.g., stars, forks, issues, and pull requests).

### 2. Update [build.ps1](file:///c:/Users/ravil/.gemini/antigravity-ide/scratch/github-clone/build.ps1)

We will rewrite the PowerShell build script to:
1. Scan the `repos/` directory.
2. For each repository folder:
    *   Read its files recursively.
    *   Construct the file path and read the text contents.
    *   Read `repo.json` to extract metadata (description, language, stars, issues, PRs).
    *   Detect if any files have been modified since the last commit in `repo.json`. If a file has been modified, **automatically append a new mock commit** (e.g., *"Update physical_file_name.py via IDE"*) with the current timestamp! This simulates a real Git commit history reflecting your IDE edits.
3. Dynamically generate the JS repository data array.
4. Bundle everything into `dist/index.html`.

---

## Verification Plan

### Manual Verification
1. Run `build.ps1` to compile the current repositories.
2. Refresh the browser at `dist/index.html` and verify the three repositories show up with their files.
3. Edit `repos/antigravity-core/README.md` in your IDE, changing some text.

# ==========================================================================
# BUILD SCRIPT - DYNAMIC COMPILATION FOR GITHUB CLONE
# Crawls local filesystem directories to build the repository database
# and bundles CSS, JS modules, and HTML into a single self-contained file.
# ==========================================================================

Write-Host "Starting build process..." -ForegroundColor Cyan

$sourceDir = "C:\Users\ravil\.gemini\antigravity-ide\scratch\github-clone"
$distDir = "$sourceDir\dist"
$reposDir = "$sourceDir\repos"

# Create dist directory if it doesn't exist
if (-not (Test-Path $distDir)) {
    New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $distDir | Out-Null
    Write-Host "Created dist directory." -ForegroundColor Green
}

# 1. Compile repositories dynamically from disk
Write-Host "Scanning local filesystem repositories in repos/..." -ForegroundColor Green
$compiledRepos = @()

if (Test-Path $reposDir) {
    $repoFolders = Get-ChildItem -Path $reposDir -Directory
    foreach ($folder in $repoFolders) {
        $repoName = $folder.Name
        $jsonPath = Join-Path $folder.FullName "repo.json"
        
        Write-Host "  Compiling repository: $repoName..."
        
        # Default fallback metadata
        $repoMeta = @{
            id = $repoName
            name = $repoName
            owner = "lamberavi"
            description = "No description provided."
            stars = 0
            forks = 0
            language = "JavaScript"
            isPrivate = $false
            updatedAt = (Get-Date -Format "yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ssZ")
            commits = @()
            issues = @()
            pullRequests = @()
        }
        
        if (Test-Path $jsonPath) {
            $jsonContent = Get-Content $jsonPath -Raw
            $repoMeta = ConvertFrom-Json $jsonContent -AsHashtable
        }
        
        # Scan files in directory (excluding repo.json)
        $files = @()
        $diskFiles = Get-ChildItem -Path $folder.FullName -File -Recurse | Where-Object { $_.Name -ne "repo.json" }
        
        $latestCommitDate = [DateTime]::MinValue
        if ($repoMeta.commits -and $repoMeta.commits.Count -gt 0) {
            foreach ($c in $repoMeta.commits) {
                if ($c.date) {
                    $d = [DateTime]::Parse($c.date)
                    if ($d -gt $latestCommitDate) {
                        $latestCommitDate = $d
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        
        $autoCommits = @()
        foreach ($file in $diskFiles) {
            $relativePath = $file.FullName.Substring($folder.FullName.Length + 1).Replace("\", "/")
            $content = Get-Content $file.FullName -Raw
            if ($null -eq $content) { $content = "" }
            
            $files += @{
                path = $relativePath
                content = $content
            }
            
            # Check modification time to auto-commit
            if ($file.LastWriteTime -gt $latestCommitDate.AddSeconds(5)) {
                $hash = [System.Guid]::NewGuid().ToString().Substring(0, 7)
                $autoCommits += @{
                    hash = $hash
                    message = "Update $relativePath via IDE"
                    author = "Ravi Lamber"
                    authorUsername = "lamberavi"
                    date = $file.LastWriteTime.ToString("yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ssZ")
                }
            }
        }
        
        # Add files to metadata
        $repoMeta.files = $files
        
        # Prepend auto commits
        if ($autoCommits.Count -gt 0) {
            $repoMeta.commits = $autoCommits + $repoMeta.commits
            $repoMeta.updatedAt = (Get-Date -Format "yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ssZ")
            
            # Save the new commits back to repo.json so they persist
            $updatedJson = $repoMeta | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 5
            $updatedJson | Out-File -FilePath $jsonPath -Encoding utf8 -Force
        }
        
        $compiledRepos += $repoMeta
    }
}

# Convert compiled repos array to JSON
$compiledReposJson = $compiledRepos | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 5

# 2. Read and process CSS
Write-Host "Processing styles.css..."
$cssContent = Get-Content "$sourceDir\styles.css" -Raw

# 3. Read and bundle JS files
Write-Host "Bundling JavaScript modules..."
$jsBundle = ""

$jsFiles = @(
    "data\mockData.js",
    "components\Navigation.js",
    "components\Sidebar.js",
    "components\Dashboard.js",
    "components\RepoHeader.js",
    "components\FileExplorer.js",
    "components\CommitList.js",
    "components\IssueTracker.js",
    "components\PullRequestTracker.js",
    "components\RepoSettings.js",
    "app.js"
)

foreach ($file in $jsFiles) {
    Write-Host "  Packing $file..."
    $content = Get-Content "$sourceDir\$file" -Raw
    
    # If this is mockData.js, inject the dynamically compiled repositories database!
    if ($file -eq "data\mockData.js") {
        $content = $content -replace "export const initialRepositories\s*=\s*\[[\s\S]*", "export const initialRepositories = $compiledReposJson;"
    }
    
    # Strip imports
    $content = $content -replace 'import\s+[\s\S]*?from\s+[''"].*?[''"];?', ''
    
    # Strip exports
    $content = $content -replace 'export\s+(const|function|class|let|var)\b', '$1'
    
    $jsBundle += "`n// --- FILE: $file ---`n" + $content + "`n"
}

# 4. Read index.html and inject styles and bundle
Write-Host "Injecting assets into index.html template..."
$htmlContent = Get-Content "$sourceDir\index.html" -Raw

# Replace CSS link with <style> block
$cssTag = '<link rel="stylesheet" href="styles.css">'
$cssReplacement = "<style>`n$cssContent`n</style>"
$htmlContent = $htmlContent.Replace($cssTag, $cssReplacement)

# Replace JS script tag with <script> block
$jsTag = '<script type="module" src="app.js"></script>'
$jsReplacement = "<script>`n$jsBundle`n</script>"
$htmlContent = $htmlContent.Replace($jsTag, $jsReplacement)

# 5. Write bundled html to dist/index.html
$targetFile = "$distDir\index.html"
$htmlContent | Out-File -FilePath $targetFile -Encoding utf8 -Force

Write-Host "Build completed successfully!" -ForegroundColor Green
Write-Host "Bundled file is available at: file:///$($targetFile.Replace('\', '/'))" -ForegroundColor Yellow

# Walkthrough - User Profile Page and Pinned Repos Grid

I have successfully designed the **User Profile View** (`github.com/lamberavi`) to look exactly like your screenshots.

---

## What was Accomplished

### 1. Header Integration and Navigation Actions
*   **Top-Right Navbar Avatar**: Bound a click event on your profile picture in the top-right navbar. Clicking it takes you directly to your **User Profile Page**!
*   **Logo/Dashboard Return**: Clicking on the GitHub logo or `Dashboard` text returns you back to the 3-column home feed view.
*   **Routing Layout Transitions**: The profile page is rendered full-width (hiding the repositories list sidebar) just like repository detail tabs, keeping the UI structure highly professional.

### 2. User Portrait & Metadata Column
*   **GitHub Public Image Redirection**: Dynamically loads your actual profile picture via your public username path (`https://github.com/lamberavi.png`), matching your screenshot.
*   **User Bio & Info**: Features your name *Ravi Lamber*, tag *lamberavi*, user bio description, and a styled full-width **Edit profile** action button.

### 3. Popular Pinned Repositories Card Grid
*   **Grid layout**: Renders the 6 popular repositories from your screenshot: `RAVI6361`, `React-portfolio-website`, `Online-Courses`, `E-Commerce`, `MusicWebsite`, and `Practice`.
*   **Interactive Cards**: Each card displays a public badge, customized description text, language dot (HTML or JavaScript), and is **completely clickable**! Clicking any card immediately navigates you to that repository's code/file explorer page inside the app.
*   **Full Sidebar Sync**: Added database folders and `repo.json` metadata configs for all 4 new repos (`RAVI6361`, `React-portfolio-website`, `Online-Courses`, `E-Commerce`) so they are fully browseable!

### 4. Contributions Calendar and Heatmap
*   **Programmatic Grid**: Compiles a 53-week heatmap calendar displaying contribution block colors (Less / More intensity scale).
*   **Screenshot Seed**: Colors a set of blocks in Nov, Dec, May, and Jun green to match the exact pattern in your screenshots.
*   **Filter Columns**: Displays year selectors (`2026`, `2025`, `2024`, `2023`) and a contribution timeline block for July 2026 stating *"lamberavi has no activity yet for this period."*

---

## How to Test and Demo (Step-by-Step)
